newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA TO USE 30-40 BLN YUAN A YEAR VS BAD DEBT.
newsitem.headline: CHINA TO USE 30-40 BLN YUAN A YEAR VS BAD DEBT.

text.p: China will set aside 30-40 billion yuan each year to write off bad debt, Dai Xianglong, governor of the People's Bank of China, the central bank, said on Thursday.
The funds would be used to clear bad debts owed by China's state enterprises to state-owned banks, Dai told a news conference.
China has set aside 30 billion yuan this year to write off bad debt.
The bank has refused to give a figure for non-performing loans and bad debt, although Chinese economists have said the full amount could take as much as a decade to clear.
The amount of unpaid interest owed to state-owned banks on loans in arrears of up to two years totalled 143.1 billion yuan at the end of June, the central bank said.
That marked an increase of 24.6 billion yuan, or 20.76 percent, from the start of the year, the People's Bank of China said.
Central bank officials say unrecoverable debts to state banks amount to about two percent of total outstanding loans.
